chunks: 3243 - Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to Shurayḥ:

O Shurayḥ, look into the cases of those given to withholding, delay, and oppression, and those who withhold the rights of people despite having means and ease, and those who channel the wealth of the Muslims to the rulers. So take the people's rights from them, and sell real estate and houses. For I heard the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم say: “The delay of a wealthy Muslim is ظلم against a Muslim.”

And whoever has no wealth, no real estate, and no house, then there is no recourse against him. And know that none can carry people upon the truth except one who restrains them from falsehood. Then treat the Muslims equally in your face, your speech, and your sitting, so that your relative may not hope for your bias, and your enemy may not despair of your justice.

And return the oath to the claimant along with evidence, for that is more clarifying against blindness and more firmly established in judgment. And know that the Muslims are upright against one another, except one flogged in a hadd who has not repented from it, or one known for false testimony, or one under suspicion.

And beware of weariness and annoyance in the judicial sitting, in which Allah, the Exalted, has made reward obligatory and made the provision therein excellent for the one who judges with truth. And appoint a term for one who claims absent witnesses between them; if he brings them, you shall take his right for him, and if he does not bring them, you shall decide the case against him.

And beware of executing a judgment in retaliation, or a hadd from the limits concerning people, or a right from the rights of Allah عزّ وجلّ, until you present that to me. And beware of sitting in the judicial assembly until you have eaten something, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.

key_terms.الْمَطْلِ: delaying payment of an owed right or debt
key_terms.الْمُوسِرِ: one who possesses wealth and financial ability
key_terms.حُقُوقَ النَّاسِ: the rights owed to other people
key_terms.حُقُوقِ اللَّهِ: rights belonging to Allah عزّ وجلّ in the legal-moral sense

ai.seo_question: What guidance did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام give Shurayḥ about justice, court procedure, and delayed debt payment?
ai.summary: This hadith records instructions from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام to Shurayḥ regarding judicial conduct, enforcement of rights, and fairness in court. It emphasizes recovery of people's rights from those with means, equal treatment of litigants, standards of testimony, and caution in issuing or carrying out serious legal judgments. It also includes a prophetic statement condemning the delayed payment of debts by a wealthy Muslim as ظلم.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3243 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from his father, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), who said to Shurayh:

"O Shurayh, observe those who procrastinate, delay payments, oppress others, and deny people their rights despite having wealth and resources. Take the rights of the people from them and sell their properties and houses if necessary.
I heard the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) say:
'Delaying payment by a wealthy Muslim is injustice to another Muslim.'

As for the one who has no wealth, property, or house, there is no recourse against him.
Know that no one can enforce the truth upon people except one who restrains them from falsehood. Treat the Muslims equally in your appearance, speech, and seating so that your relatives do not hope for favoritism, nor do your enemies despair of your justice.

Return the oath to the claimant along with evidence, for this is clearer for truth and firmer in judgment.
Know that Muslims are trustworthy over one another, except for one who has been punished for a crime and has not repented, one who is known for false testimony, or one who is under suspicion.

Beware of irritation and annoyance in the court, which Allah (swt) has made a place of reward and the best form of provision for those who judge with justice.
Grant the claimant time to bring witnesses if they are absent. If he produces them, give him his right, and if not, decide the case against him.

Beware of executing a judgment involving retaliation, legal punishments, or any right of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, without presenting it to me first.
And do not sit in the court until you have eaten something, if Allah (swt) wills."
